item.title: FracturedJson
item.description:
📝 Long arrays are written with multiple items per line across multiple lines. { "AttackPlans": [ { "TeamId": 1, "Spawns": [ { "Time": 0, "UnitType": "Grunt", "SpawnPointIndex": 0 }, { "Time": 0, "UnitType": "Grunt", "SpawnPointIndex": 0 }, { "Time": 0, "UnitType": "Grunt", "SpawnPointIndex": 0 } ] } ], "DefensePlans": [ { "TeamId": 2, "Placements": [ { "UnitType": "Archer", "Position": [ 41, 7 ] }, { "UnitType": "Pikeman", "Position": [ 40, 7 ] }, { "UnitType": "Barricade", "Position": [ 39, 7 ] } ] } ] } FracturedJson tries to format data like a person would. { "AttackPlans" : [ { "TeamId": 1, "Spawns": [ {"Time": 0, "UnitType": "Grunt", "SpawnPointIndex": 0}, {"Time": 0, "UnitType": "Grunt", "SpawnPointIndex": 0}, {"Time": 0, "UnitType": "Grunt", "SpawnPointIndex": 0} ] } ], "DefensePlans": [ { "TeamId" : 2, "Placements": [ { "UnitType": "Archer", "Position": [41, 7] }, { "UnitType": "Pikeman", "Position": [40, 7] }, { "UnitType": "Barricade", "Position": [39, 7] } ] } ] } How It Works FracturedJson uses four types of formatting: inlined, compact multiline array, table and expanded.
🔗 Read more: https://github.com/j-brooke/FracturedJson/wiki

item.title: Assorted less(1) tips
item.description:
📝 You can add that header-file to the argument list with :e file. So using 3141G will jump to line 3141. Find the next line that doesn't match the pattern * search across multiple files, starting from the current location in the current file @ rewind to the first file and search from there @* rewind to the first file and search from there across multiple files Thus you would use /@*«pattern» to search for "pattern" starting with the first file.
🔗 Read more: https://blog.thechases.com/posts/assorted-less-tips/
